children: Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar has been hailed as a hero by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, US President Donald Trump and Prime Minister Narendra Modi after he helped avert a potentially catastrophic incident aboard a Flydubai flight bound for Tel Aviv.

Machchhar, the captain of Flydubai Flight FZ1073, was seriously injured after his Omani co-pilot allegedly attacked him in the cockpit during the flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv on Wednesday. Despite his injuries, Machchhar managed to open the cockpit door, allowing passengers and crew to enter and restrain the attacker. The aircraft subsequently made an emergency landing in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia. The flight was carrying 174 people.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu described Machchhar as a “true hero”, saying his actions prevented a major disaster. In remarks reported after the incident, Netanyahu said the Indian pilot had been attacked with an axe by the co-pilot and, despite being wounded, managed to unlock the cockpit door. The precise circumstances and motive behind the attack remain under investigation.
Netanyahu also drew a comparison with the September 11, 2001 attacks, saying the actions of Machchhar and others aboard the aircraft helped prevent another 9/11-style tragedy.

US President Donald Trump also praised Machchhar, calling him a “hero” and highlighting the fact that he managed to open the cockpit door despite being badly injured. Trump said he had discussed the incident with Netanyahu.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi separately praised Machchhar for his courage and resolve.

“Captain Smit Machchhar is a HERO,” Modi said in a post, adding that despite being seriously injured, the pilot showed immense courage and helped save hundreds of lives and avert a major tragedy. Modi also expressed his wishes for Machchhar's speedy recovery.

According to reports, passengers and off-duty pilots on board subsequently helped overpower the co-pilot and assist in stabilising the aircraft. An Israeli passenger also helped operate the aircraft before the emergency landing in Saudi Arabia.

Machchhar, an Indian national from Mumbai, has more than 13 years of commercial aviation experience and around 9,750 flying hours, primarily on Boeing 737 aircraft. He previously worked with SpiceJet before joining Flydubai.
The co-pilot, an Omani national, has been taken into custody by Saudi authorities. Investigators are examining the circumstances surrounding the cockpit attack and the motive behind it.

Machchhar is currently recovering in Saudi Arabia after receiving medical treatment for his injuries. The incident has also prompted scrutiny of aviation security procedures, while Flydubai has temporarily suspended flights between the UAE and Israel as the investigation continues.
